### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was not observed at all in the earlier window (0 occurrences in 200 traces). In the later window it appears in about 30 in 100 traces (59 of 200), averages roughly 0.65 occurrences per trace, repeats within about 14 in 100 traces, and sits around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.41). [OCC001, POS001]
- The routing out of A12 changed: earlier, A12's observed outgoing transitions split between A04 (about 52%) and A13 (about 48%); in the later window, all observed outgoing transitions of A12 go to A01. [DIR002]
- In the later window, A01's observed outgoing transitions go to A04 (about 53%) and A13 (about 47%) — closely matching the split A12 showed earlier. [DIR001]
- A01 moved from never co-occurring with the other activities to co-occurring in about 30 in 100 traces with each of A04, A13 and A12. In the later window A12 never appears without A01 (earlier, A12 appeared without A01 in about 33 in 100 traces), with A12 preceding A01 in about 16 in 100 traces and the two interleaving or repeating in about 14 in 100; A01 and A04, and A01 and A13, show no fixed order, appearing interleaved or repeated in about 30 in 100 traces each. [REL001, REL002, REL003]
- Pairwise distances shifted consistently with one extra step in this loop: A12 to A04 and A12 to A13 moved from typically 1–2 event positions apart to typically 2–3; repetitions of A12 moved from about 4 to about 5 positions apart, and repetitions of A04 and A13 shifted from lags of 3–5 towards 4–5. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, A01 executes as an added step between A12 and its successors A04 and A13. Earlier, traces running this part of the process went from A12 directly to A04 (about 52%) or A13 (about 48%); in the later window A12 leads to A01, and A01 continues to A04 (about 53%) or A13 (about 47%), reproducing the earlier split one position later. A01 runs only in the roughly 30 in 100 traces that contain A12, always together with A12, and the distances from A12 to A04/A13 and between repeated loop executions lengthened by about one event position, as expected if a step was inserted into the loop. [DIR001, DIR002, OCC001, POS001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

Twelve evidence items qualified against an expectation of about 0.17 items without change, so the set as a whole is far larger than random re-splits of unchanged behaviour would produce; the items are, however, largely views of one underlying rerouting and are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window only shows A01 was not observed there, so an extremely rare earlier variant cannot be fully excluded, although A12's complete rerouting and the coordinated lengthening of the lags make pure sampling noise unlikely. Positions and lags are measured in event positions, not clock time, so no conclusion about timing is drawn; the rerouting concerns only the subset of traces containing A12, and direction shares are over outgoing transitions rather than cases.

Other differences: A12 was observed slightly less in the later window (about 33 in 100 traces earlier versus about 30 in 100 later, with 175 versus 131 observed outgoing transitions); this small decrease could reflect sampling variation. [DIR002, REL002]
